I have a tattoo, across my back - shoulder blade to shoulder blade. It is Jefferson Davis, Gen. Lee and Stonewall Jackson on horses, also known as the Stone Mounain carving. It was done by one of the best American tattoo artists, Russ Abbott.

Having lived in Atlanta, GA, I spent nearly every weekend in Stone Mountain park, jogging or hiking. So this carving was the best symbol of my life in the US I could think of.

  • Any story? I got it on short notice, only three days before my flight back to Europe. In the morning of that day, I had oral surgery, so when I came to get the tattoo done, I still couldn't feel a thing. As soon as I tell her what it is and what it means to me, she says "Ok, well it was nice talking to you". I was floored. I didn't know that people are still so vehemently opposed to them, especially in their mid-late 20s. Oh well, her loss.

Even before I got mine, I was against people walking into a tattoo parlor, picking one out of a book, and getting one for the sake of having a tattoo. If you're going to get one, get it because it means something important to you, because it isn't going anywhere. I know people who have dolphins on their ankles "because it's cute", people who have their friends' band logos that are neither existent nor liked anymore, and people who got quotes/words, and those are all things that I think are tacky. People sag when they get older. Words and faces won't look good when things sag. If you're going to get one, imagine what it looks like when it fades a little bit, has a slight blue/green shade if it's black, and what it's going to look like with moles, scars, stretch marks and the gods know what else. Does it still sound as if it'll look good? Good enough to still let people see it, and not be ashamed of your decisions in the past? Great. Do your research on a good artist, and go do it. Otherwise, don't. Seriously.

ALSO: If you can't cover it up with formal clothes, think twice. Many employers won't hire you, no matter how skilled you are if you have a tattoo (anything) that you can't cover up. Having hand/neck/face/lip tattoos basically screams "I don't want to have a tax-paying job". If you don't or can't work for yourself, think twice. Think four times. Think about it a hundred times.
